text:
Noah: Hi team — got a $2,100 bill from an ER I visited while traveling. Hospital is out-of-network and billed full charges. I told them it was emergency care but they say that doesn’t change anything. How do I avoid the balance bill?
Priya (People Ops): Sorry you’re dealing with that. Emergency services have special protections sometimes. Quick steps: 1) get the ER itemized bill + claim EOB from the carrier; 2) ask the hospital to apply the "emergency services" billing code and reprocess; 3) send docs to benefits so we can file an external review if needed. DM docs and I’ll triage.
Noah: I have the itemized bill but no EOB yet. I called the insurer and they showed a denial reason: "out-of-network provider." They said they processed at out-of-network allowed amount and paid $600, leaving me $1,500 balance.
Rosa (Benefits): If the carrier paid an out-of-network amount, we need that EOB. Also, under the federal emergency services rules, if the service was a true emergency the plan often must cover as if in-network for cost-sharing — you may be eligible for a partial or full balance adjustment. Attach the EOB and bill and email benefits@redwood.com with subject "ER out-of-network dispute - Noah".
Noah: Uploaded the itemized bill and the insurer call reference number to the DM. No EOB PDF yet, they said they mailed it. Is a call reference enough?
Priya (People Ops): Call reference helps but we prefer the official EOB. You can request an expedited EOB via carrier phone or secure portal; ask them to email it or provide a claim number we can use. In the meantime, ask the hospital billing to put the account on hold — say you’re pursuing an insurance appeal and request a 60-day hold.
Provider Billing: Hello Noah, billing team here. We can put a 60-day hold if you provide the claim number and insurer contact. If you have an authorization note or ER triage record we can attach to support "emergency" classification.
Noah: Hospital placed the hold. I don’t have an ER triage note yet — how do I get that?
Priya (People Ops): Contact the hospital — ask medical records for the ED visit summary or triage note. They usually send it within a few days. Send it to benefits@redwood.com once you have it. Also copy me and Rosa so we can coordinate with the carrier.
benefits-bot: Emergency billing resource: https://benefits.redwood.com/emergency-billing-guidance.pdf. Required attachments for dispute: itemized bill, EOB, ED visit summary, claim number, hospital contact. Submit to benefits@redwood.com.
Rosa (Benefits): Once we have the EOB + ED summary we will: 1) file an internal appeal with the carrier asking for in-network parity under emergency protections; 2) if denied, request external review/independent dispute resolution and contact the state DOI if applicable. We’ll also request provider billing adjustment while appeal is pending.
Noah: Carrier emailed the EOB PDF (claim # CN-334455). I just sent everything to benefits@redwood.com with subject "ER out-of-network dispute - Noah" and CC’d Priya. Thanks for quick help.
Rosa (Benefits): Got it — I’ll open the appeal and mark priority. If it’s denied after internal appeal we’ll escalate to external review. Will update here when I hear from carrier. :thumbsup:
